analysis: Reviewed all units. Changes: (1) docs/operations/provider-release.md is a documentation update (0.9.21 candidate note, v0.9.20 published). It keeps the release authorization, signed-tag, hash-pinned registration and revocation controls described in the threat model and adds no new secrets or steps. (2) libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump from 53d9647 to 5c2ff51. Its contents are not visible, so it is a coverage limit. The docs say it pins the ordinary-request retirement API (mlx-swift-lm #305). Later passes should check the engine retirement, cancellation and KV/prefix-cache cleanup paths (T-010, T-028, T-041) if that source is supplied. (3) EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift (head line 57, 73-75) adds a stored measurementPurpose with a default of .serving on EnginePrefillReceipt. The EngineMeasurementPurpose type is defined elsewhere and not visible here. Nothing consumes the field in the visible code. The expected use is to keep calibration samples out of serving throughput learning. A later pass should confirm that calibration receipts are created with a non-serving purpose, and that the default of .serving does not let calibration or health-check traffic poison coordinator-visible rate evidence. (4) EngineV2Bridge+CalibrationPrompt.swift renames mimoCalibrationPrompt to modelCalibrationPrompt. The prompt stays built-in and never comes from customer data (head lines 4-6). (5) EngineV2Bridge+Lifecycle.swift line 161 renames cancelMimoCalibration to cancelModelCalibration inside shutdown(). The ordering is unchanged: the calibration task is cancelled and awaited. Callers and definitions of the renamed symbols are outside this batch, and the calibration generalization to all ordinary engines is not visible. Calibration now runs without customer jobs, so integration should check that it is gated against active serving traffic, runs on bounded resources and cannot be triggered remotely. No concrete security regression is visible in the supplied diffs.
